# Difference of balls, one-limb center

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/, results/milestone1/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `ball_sub_1_full` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

A ball $Z$, of center $c_w$ and radius $r_w$, that contains $x - y$ for every $x \in X, y \in Y$, with $X$ the ball of center $c_x$ and radius $r_x$ and $Y$ the ball of center $c_y$ and radius $r_y$. A ball may also be the whole line or the empty set.

$$Z \supseteq \{\, x - y : x \in X, y \in Y \,\}.$$

## C++

| Form | Operands | Result | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `X - Y` | `Ball<T, 1>`, `Ball<T, 1>` | `Ball<T, 1>` |  |
| `X -= Y` | `Ball<T, 1>`, `Ball<T, 1>` | `Ball<T, 1>` |  |
| `X - a` | `Ball<T, 1>`, `T` | `Ball<T, 1>` | the point is the ball of radius 0 its constructor makes |
| `a - X` | `T`, `Ball<T, 1>` | `Ball<T, 1>` | the point is the ball of radius 0 its constructor makes |
| `X - c` | `Ball<T, 1>`, `Expansion<T, 1>` | `Ball<T, 1>` | the point is the ball of radius 0 its constructor makes |
| `c - X` | `Expansion<T, 1>`, `Ball<T, 1>` | `Ball<T, 1>` | the point is the ball of radius 0 its constructor makes |
| `X -= a` | `Ball<T, 1>`, `T` | `Ball<T, 1>` | the point is the ball of radius 0 its constructor makes |
| `X -= c` | `Ball<T, 1>`, `Expansion<T, 1>` | `Ball<T, 1>` | the point is the ball of radius 0 its constructor makes |

`T` is `float` or `double`; the operations are in namespace `kairn`, header `kairn/kairn.hpp`. The operators and functions also accept the marker `kairn::unverified` on an operand, which they need while the kernel is UNVERIFIED.

## Requires

- $X$, of center $c_x$ and radius $r_x$, is a canonical ball: a finite ball (finite center, finite radius $\ge 0$), the whole line (center 0, radius $+\infty$), or the empty set (every limb a NaN).
- $Y$, of center $c_y$ and radius $r_y$, is a canonical ball: a finite ball (finite center, finite radius $\ge 0$), the whole line (center 0, radius $+\infty$), or the empty set (every limb a NaN).

## Guarantees

For operands that satisfy the requirements, finite, infinite or NaN:

- **B1.** The result $Z$, of center $c_w$ and radius $r_w$, is a canonical ball: a finite ball, the whole line (center 0, radius $+\infty$), or the empty set (every limb a NaN).
- **B2.** $Z$ is empty exactly when an operand ball is empty.
- **B3.** If $Z$ is a finite ball, then $X$ and $Y$ are finite balls, and $\lvert (x - y) - c_w\rvert \le r_w$ for all real $x$ and $y$ with $\lvert x - c_x\rvert \le r_x$, $\lvert y - c_y\rvert \le r_y$.
- **B4.** No condition under which $Z$ is a finite ball is claimed yet: the claims list none, which does not say that it always is.
- It follows that in every case $Z$ contains $x - y$ for every $x \in X$, $y \in Y$: the whole line contains every real number, and an empty operand has no points.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 2 bits, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the IEEE model, with signed zeros, infinities, NaN and overflow. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `ball_sub_1_full_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/IeeeBallCores.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/IeeeBallCores.v); `make -C proofs` finds no axiom in its proof beyond the four allowed ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md)).

## Source

**Algorithm:** ball_sub_1, then the fix-up of the special states of a ball (Milestone 1 listing). **License:** core: as ball_sub_1; fix-up: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/ball_sub_1_full.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/ball_sub_1_full.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal model (`proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).
It calls [`ball_sub_1`](ball_sub_1.md).

```
# The difference of balls with one-limb centers, with the special states of a ball:
# ball_sub_1, then the fix-up of milestone1.md, "Ball kernels".

(cz, rz) = ball_sub_1(cx, rx, cy, ry)
q        = add(rx, ry)
e        = eq(q, q)
a        = abs(cz)
f1       = lt(a, const inf)
f2       = lt(rz, const inf)
f        = and(f1, f2)
c0       = select(f, cz, 0)
r        = select(f, rz, const inf)
cw       = select(e, c0, q)
rw       = select(e, r, q)
```

## Not claimed

- Anything for operands that do not satisfy the requirements.
- The sign of a zero limb, and which NaN a NaN result is: the claims compare neither.
